m0-context.imperative: Read your inherited global doctrine (this skill's references/global-crew.md and references/global-everyone.md), then the project deltas if present: docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md, docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md, plus the handoff and the relevant packet. postconditions.satisfied_by: Read complete global crew/everyone doctrine, checklist-engine MCP reference, project CREW_CONTEXT/GLOSSARY, assigned g1c handoff, and map/INDEX.md plus scripts.run_crew symbol packet. Handoff includes task, protected intent, two-file scope/exclusions, required evidence, TDD mode, stop conditions, and result path.

m1.title: <implementation step>
m1.imperative: <make the minimal change for this step>. Attest any check:null precondition BEFORE start — the engine refuses `start <id>` while a precondition is unmet, so the order is attest-precondition -> start (the refusal is non-destructive; just attest, then retry). TDD when the test mode requires it, red -> green -> refactor: encode the RED step as a check:null postcondition (manual attest of 'new test written and observed failing') — NOT a command check, because a command check would run the by-design-failing test and block the gate; keep the GREEN step as the command check. For a test-after/inspection run, collapse to the single green/observable postcondition (c2).

why_trail.why: Context establishes a strictly bounded TDD repair: make crew_cwd absolute for every non-None path while preserving legacy None; cover real default-dot dispatch and resume; edit only scripts/run_crew.py and tests/test_crew_worktree_cwd.py, then write the prescribed result artifact.

The new default-dot dispatch and resume tests failed against the pre-repair resolver because it returned relative Path('.'), then passed after crew_cwd began resolving relative root first and relative worktree beneath it. The exact focused suite is green with 171 tests, while the legacy None branch remains unchanged.
